expected.summary: Twenty two minutes before the anchor a planned switchover for host maintenance (MAINT-1184) promoted inventory-db-b and demoted inventory-db-a to a read-only standby. inventory's connections were terminated, and every pod reconnected to inventory-db.internal using a cached DNS entry that still pointed at the old primary's address, 10.0.4.17. Every reservation write on those pods now fails with cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction (SQLSTATE 25006), so inventory.reserve returns 500. Each pod heals when its DNS cache entry (ttl 1800s) expires and it re-resolves to 10.0.4.23, so the pods recover one by one, nine to thirty six minutes after the switchover, and the error rate falls in steps; at the anchor inventory-4, inventory-5 and inventory-6 are still failing. cart calls inventory without retry and does not treat it as optional, so GET /cart and POST /checkout fail with 502s that propagate through checkout and web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. No inventory code or version changed. shipping's rollout from 1.4.2 to 1.5.1, three minutes before the switchover, is a red herring: shipping shows no errors and the failures are all read-only write errors on inventory.
contributingFactors: inventory's resolver caching the database address for thirty minutes, so pods reconnected to the demoted primary
the switchover demoting the old primary to a read-only standby that still accepts connections
cart treating inventory reservations as required, so write failures fail whole carts and checkouts

criteria.description: Does the brief name inventory writing to the demoted, read-only inventory-db-a after the planned switchover, because its cached DNS entry still points at the old primary, with cart and checkout failures reaching edge-gateway? 5 = the switchover, the read-only errors, the stale address and the victim chain. Saying only 'inventory-db is down' scores at most 3; blaming the shipping rollout scores 1.

Is it grounded in the SQLSTATE 25006 errors naming the old address, the switchover notice and reconnect logs at onset, and the per-pod DNS refresh logs that line up with each pod recovering? Cap at 3 unless it explains why pods recover one at a time.
Does it dismiss shipping's 1.5.1 rollout with evidence (no shipping errors), avoid blaming cart, checkout or edge-gateway, and note that the problem is clearing on its own but not yet on every pod?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
